Shell.claim: Where the camps walk together — and where exactly they don't
Shell.footer: Common Ground is part of the open-source project policy. Every number comes from real consultation data; every processing step is audit-logged.

Catalog.title: The dispute, made readable
Catalog.lead: A public consultation brings hundreds of submissions — and leaves the real question open: what does everyone agree on, and where exactly do opinions part? Common Ground answers this per consultation: with the camps, their common path, and the point where it forks.

Consultation.statLine: {submissions} submissions · {participants} participants · {points} claims and objections · {votes} votes
Consultation.inferredNote: {inferred} of the {votes} votes were inferred from the free-text submissions and are marked as such.
Consultation.chainIntro: Behind every proposal stands the same chain of reasoning: a reading of the situation, a prognosis of the effect, the goal, a value judgment — and from these, the measure. For each stage, the chain shows how strongly each camp carries that stage's claims. This makes visible how far both camps walk the same path — and at which stage it forks.
Consultation.measuresIntro: A bill is rarely a single decision. The analysis splits it into separately decidable parts — each with a chain of its own. What holds for the proposal as a whole is above; here is where each sub-decision stands on its own.
Consultation.doorsIntro: Against a proposed measure there are exactly five kinds of objection — no more. Every submitted objection was assigned to one of these five questions, and the proposed solutions from the submissions to the question they answer. This turns a pile of criticism into a checklist.
Consultation.doorSolutions: {n, plural, one {one proposed solution} other {# proposed solutions}}
Consultation.doorSolutionsHeading: Proposed solutions answering this question first ({n})
Consultation.methodStep1: Every submission is read in full and decomposed into individual claims, objections, and proposals — with source quote and location.
Consultation.methodStep2: Each claim is editorially reviewed and assigned to a stage of the reasoning chain; each objection to one of the five objection kinds.
Consultation.methodStep3: The claims are voted on — partly directly, partly inferred from the free texts and marked as such.
Consultation.methodStep4: Those who vote alike form a camp. Camps emerge computationally from voting behavior, not from self-assignment.
Consultation.methodStep5: For each stage and each sub-decision, the analysis compares how strongly each camp carries it — yielding the common path and the breakpoint.
Consultation.notFound: This consultation has not been fully analyzed yet.
